div.head: II Atr 6.1
div.ab: Æt eallum slyht ⁊ æt ealre ðære hergunge ⁊ æt eallum ðam hearmum, ðe ær ðam gedon wære, ær ðæt frið geset wære, man eall onweig læte, ⁊ nan man þæt ne rece ne bote ne bidde.
De omni homicidio et omni robaria et omnibus incendiis, que facta sunt antequam pax fuerat instituta, totum dimittatur, et nemo uindictam uel emendationem exigat.
Æt eallum slyht ⁊ æt ealre ðære hergunge ⁊ æt eallum ðam hearmum ðe ær ðam gedon wære, ær ðæt frið geset wære, man eall onweig læte, ⁊ nan man þæt ne rece ne bote ne bidde.

Von jedem Todtschlag und aller jener Verheerung und allen jenen Schädigungen, die ehedem verübt war[en], bevor dieser Friedensschluss festgesetzt wurde, werde alles [hinfort] bei Seite gelassen, und niemand räche das oder fordere Busszahlung [dafür].

Concerning every killing and all that harrying and all those injuries which were done before this peace was established, let everything be set aside [henceforth], and let no one avenge it or ask compensation [for it].

As regards all the slaughter and all the harrying and all the injuries which were done before the truce was made—all of them shall be forgotten, and no-one shall avenge them or demand compensation for them.

Concerning all the slaughter and all the harrying and all the injuries which were committed before the truce was established, all of them are to be dismissed, and no one is to avenge it or ask for compensation.

note.seg: Q scheint in hearm h als b, m als n verlesen und an bærn- (ing, -es, -et) ‘Brand’ gedacht zu haben.—In Z. 2 ist, laut Q's sunt, vielleicht wære in wæren zu emendieren; sonst muss þe ‘was’ heissen

Q seems to have misread, in hearm, h as b and m as n, and to have thought of bærn- (ing, -es, -et) ‘burning’. — In l. 2, in view of Q’s sunt, wære should perhaps be emended to wæren; otherwise þe must mean ‘which’

Durch Ld Q ist wrece für lq gesichert; rece in B ist auch nur daraus zu deuten, vielleicht als Nord. Schreibung; denn recce, was Schreibfehler B's voraussetzen würde, heisst ‘kümmere sich, beachte’, Gen. regierend, oder ‘erkläre’: was beides nicht passt. Vielmehr sind Rache (s. Gl Strafe 4) und Busse (s. d. Gl 5a) die beiden Arten der Gutmachung einer Missetat

wrece is assured for lq by Ld Q; rece in B too can only be explained from it, perhaps as a Norse spelling; for recce, which a scribal error of B’s would presuppose, means ‘care for, heed’, governing the gen., or ‘explain’: neither of which fits. Rather, vengeance (see Gl Strafe 4) and compensation (see that word in Gl 5a) are the two ways of making amends for a misdeed
Q’s reading incendiis would seem to be based on some form like bærnum for brynum in the A.S. MS source.
gedon wære, cf. facta sunt, Q. Liebermann suggests emending the A.S. reading to wæren.
